label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, poison-message, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 7 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER idempotent (unchanged), LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS retry -> dead_letter); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

case.title: The ledger stops booking: a poison message

alert.name: BooksBehindProvider
alert.summary: Our books cannot catch up with the provider: at each of the last 2 evaluations, the money check waited 15 s and could not settle up to its cutoff. At the last one, messages up to it were not handled yet: ledger 129.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was redeployed at 20:36:17 with BAD_EVENTS=retry. About 3 s later, provider event evt_000282 landed at provider-events/1@129 with an invalid amount ('amount must be positive integer cents'). payment-confirmer, which runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, dead-lettered that event and kept going. ledger-consumer instead retries the same message forever, backing off up to every 15 s, and never commits past offset 129. While it is stuck, lag grows on all three partitions, so the consumer appears blocked as a whole. The money check therefore cannot settle up to its cutoff ('ledger 129'). The trigger is a malformed event. The outage itself comes from the retry-forever policy on the ledger, which lets one poison message stop all booking.

evidence.shows: ledger-consumer keeps retrying provider-events/1@129: attempts 3 to 9, the same error each time ('amount must be positive integer cents'), with retry_in_seconds rising to 15.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 20:36:17 with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent and BAD_EVENTS=retry. payment-confirmer runs BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter. payments-api still has CHARGE_AMOUNT_UNIT=cents.
payment-confirmer dead-lettered the same message, provider-events/1@129, at 20:36:20 for the same invalid-amount reason, so its own processing went on.

The trace for evt_000282 runs: webhook-receiver accepted it and queued it to partition 1, offset 129. ledger-consumer then logged repeated will_retry errors on it for over 60 s, and payment-confirmer dead-lettered it.
Consumer lag was 0 until about 20:36:29, then rose steadily on partitions 0, 1 and 2, reaching 83 to 87 by 20:37:44. The backlog is growing.
Ledger 'posted' and 'already_processed' rates are still above zero. A dead_lettered outcome appears only for payment-confirmer, not for the ledger.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings from before the 20:36:17 deploy. These are presumably BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter, but the deploy log decides. That should dead-letter the poison event at offset 129 and let the ledger work through the backlog. Then look into evt_000282 in the dead-letter queue: compare its amount with the provider's records, and book or repair it by hand. Finally, run the money check with wait=true and confirm the books settle.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated, and lag grows a little during that time. Once the event is dead-lettered, evt_000282 stays unbooked in the ledger, so the money check may flag a missing posting until someone handles it by hand. Open points: I have not confirmed the earlier settings, or why the provider sent an event with an invalid amount. If the earlier setting was not dead_letter, the rollback may not unblock the consumer.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Redeploy ledger-consumer with the current settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, BAD_EVENTS=retry). It will resume retrying from its committed offset. The ledger is idempotent, so reprocessing does not double-book.
